channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Immigration – Habeas corpus
item.description: Where a petitioner who was ordered removed to Vietnam in 2002 following a state criminal conviction was taken into custody in November 2025, the redetention of the petitioner violates 8 C.F.R. §241.13, so he should be immediately released subject to the conditions in his preexisting order of supervision.

item.title: Judges – Quasi-judicial immunity – Receiver
item.description: Where a court-appointed receiver that took control of a memory care assisted living facility’s operations and assets has moved to dismiss a complaint brought against it, that motion should be allowed because the receiver is protected by quasi-judicial immunity due to its performance of judicial functions.

item.title: Banks and banking – Zelle – Chapter 93A
item.description: Where plaintiffs have brought suit under the Massachusetts Consumer Protection Act (G.L.c. 93A), the defendants’ motion to dismiss should be allowed despite the plaintiffs’ claim that the defendants violated Chapter 93A by falsely claiming that sending money via a money-transfer mobile application known as Zelle was safe.

item.title: Jurisdiction – Choice of law – Chapter 93A
item.description: Where a defendant insurance company that allegedly violated G.L.c. 93A and 176D has filed a motion to dismiss, the motion should be allowed based on a choice of law provision in the plaintiff’s policy.

item.title: Appeals – Mandamus
item.description: Where a single justice denied a petition for relief in the nature of mandamus, there was no abuse of discretion or error of law, as the petitioner has failed to show that she could not obtain review of the denial of her requested transfer on appeal following final judgment or in a petition for interlocutory relief.

item.title: Appeals – G.L.c. 211, §3
item.description: Where a Housing Court judge allowed a respondent’s motion for a preliminary injunction and ordered the petitioner to cease and desist from continuing to reside in his father's apartment, it was not error for a single justice to denying the petitioner relief pursuant to G.L.c. 211, §3, as the petitioner has not made, and cannot make, a showing that he has no adequate alternative remedy.

item.title: Criminal – Sentencing
item.description: Where a defendant has challenged the substantive and procedural reasonableness of his above-guidelines sentence of 144 months, the defendant has not identified anything to suggest that the sentence was not supported by a plausible rationale or was not a defensible result.

item.title: Employment – Fee reduction – Title VII
item.description: Where a plaintiff who won a jury verdict on a retaliation claim under Title VII has challenged the trial judge’s decision to reduce her counsel fees, it was not an abuse of discretion for the judge to exclude “generic” time entries from the lodestar calculation and to reduce the award by 20 percent based on the plaintiff's limited success.

item.title: Immigration – Persecution
item.description: Where the Board of Immigration Appeals affirmed the denial of a petitioner’s applications for asylum, withholding of removal, and protection under the Convention Against Torture, her petition for review should be denied because the petitioner did not carry her burden of establishing that she (1) experienced past persecution or (2) has a well-founded fear of future persecution upon removal to Brazil.

item.title: Bankruptcy – Loss of assets – Discharge denial
item.description: Where a U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge found that appellant debtors did not satisfactorily explain the disposition of their assets and consequentially denied them a discharge, that decision should be affirmed despite the debtors’ argument that 11 U.S.C. §727(a)(5) only permits denial of a discharge when the lost assets at issue are substantial.
